record.paper_title: Collective Phenomena in the LiHoxY1−xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet: Recent Progress and Open Questions
record.original_question: Do transverse-field-induced random fields in diluted ferromagnetic LiHoxY1−xF4, for example at Ho concentration x = 0.44, produce Griffiths singularity effects in the paramagnetic regime just above the ferromagnetic transition temperature Tc, and what systematic experimental investigation is needed to test the claimed susceptibility-scaling behavior?

evidence.quote: Finally, we note that the presence of induced random fields has been invoked to interpret the transverse field and temperature dependence (e.g. scaling behavior) of the magnetic susceptibility in LiHoxY1−xF4 (x = 0.44).

In particular, these random fields have been postulated to give rise to Griffiths' singularity effects in the paramagnetic regime at temperatures just above Tc [69]. It would be useful to explore this claim further.
In fact, a systematic experimental investigation of the fascinating physics of random field systems in the diluted ferromagnetic regime of LiHoxY1−xF4 is probably warranted.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the diluted dipolar Ising magnet LiHo_xY_{1-x}F_4, in which magnetic Ho^{3+} ions (Ising-like, with easy axis along the crystallographic c-direction) are randomly substituted by non-magnetic Y^{3+} ions at concentration 1-x. When a magnetic field B_x is applied transverse to the Ising axis, the combination of B_x-induced off-diagonal admixing of crystal-field states and the dilution-induced loss of local crystalline symmetry generates, through the long-range dipolar couplings, effective random longitudinal fields acting on the Ising degrees of freedom. Fix the Ho concentration x = 0.44, which lies in the diluted ferromagnetic regime with a finite ferromagnetic transition temperature T_c(B_x) > 0 for sufficiently small B_x.

(a) Determine whether the transverse-field-induced random longitudinal fields produce Griffiths-type singularities in the paramagnetic phase at temperatures just above T_c(B_x); that is, decide whether the linear and nonlinear magnetic susceptibilities exhibit non-analytic Griffiths behavior (e.g. essential singularities or power-law tails associated with rare large ferromagnetic clusters in the random-field environment) for T just above T_c(B_x).

(b) Identify the precise scaling form of the magnetic susceptibility χ(T, B_x) as a function of temperature and transverse field that would be predicted by such a random-field Griffiths scenario, and specify how this scaling could be distinguished experimentally from non-Griffiths smearing of the transition.
artifact.status_search_result: The question was raised as an open problem calling for further experimental and theoretical investigation. Subsequent work (e.g. numerical linked-cluster studies of Griffiths–McCoy singularities in the dilute transverse-field Ising model, Phys. Rev. E 99, 032129 (2019), and observations in related random quantum Ising magnets such as PrTiNbO6) has explored Griffiths phenomena in similar models, but no definitive systematic experimental confirmation of the proposed Griffiths singularity scaling of the susceptibility in LiHo_{0.44}Y_{0.56}F_4 just above T_c has been established. The status thus appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Griffiths-McCoy singularities in the dilute transverse-field Ising model
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical linked cluster expansion study of Griffiths-McCoy singularities in dilute transverse-field Ising models.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical/numerical work on Griffiths singularities in dilute transverse-field Ising models continues, but does not directly confirm the LiHo_{0.44}Y_{0.56}F_4 experimental scaling claim.

status_evidence.title: Spin dynamics and Griffiths singularity in the random quantum Ising magnet PrTiNbO6
status_evidence.snippet: Observation of Griffiths singularity in a related random quantum Ising magnet.
status_evidence.claim: Griffiths phenomena have been investigated in analogous magnets, indicating the LiHoYF4 question remains an active research direction.

status_evidence.title: Induced Random Fields in the LiHoxY1-xF4 Quantum Ising Magnet in a Transverse Magnetic Field
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of induced random fields and their possible role in producing Griffiths singularities in the paramagnetic regime above T_c.
status_evidence.claim: The Griffiths-singularity interpretation has been postulated but calls for further systematic experimental verification.
